messages:
sara_cs: FYI — ACME reported Invoice extractor failing after today's rollout. Their downstream parser is breaking because some numeric fields are coming back as words (e.g., '2' -> 'two'). They say internal evals passed.
max_engineer: Can you paste the exact customer prompt + model output sample? Need something to reproduce.
sara_cs: Pasted from the ACME support thread (redacted):
ACME: "Prompt: Extract order_table from receipt text. Output must be a JSON array of objects with keys: id (string), qty (integer), price_cents (integer), currency (string)."
ACME: "Model output (snip): [{\"id\": \"A1\", \"qty\": \"two\", \"price_cents\": \"120000\", \"currency\": \"USD\"}, ...]" — qty is text. Their parser expects integer and fails.
eli_se: Hmm — our internal eval harness uses function schemas and enforcement which coerces/validates types; we probably didn't have a raw-text case in the eval set. If the model's wording tendency changed, it wouldn't show up in our tests.
leo_research: Quick hypothesis: a recent prompt tweak added a 'humanize numbers for readability' guideline in the assistant/system prompt. That would affect structured responses if not scoped properly.
deploy_bot: Canary rollout 0xabc3 applied -> 40% of traffic (regions: us-east-1, us-west-2).
max_engineer: Repro steps I'm going to run: 1) send the exact raw receipt text ACME used via /v1/chat/completions with model "redwood-v2-240b" 2) include same function schema and temperature=0.0 3) ensure no client-side post-processing. If I can reproduce, we know it's model prompt behavior.
sara_cs: ACME already tried temp=0.0 and saw the same. They pasted their API snippet:
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "redwood-v2-240b",
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful extractor."},
    {"role":"user","content":"<raw receipt text>"}
  ],
  "functions": [ {"name":"order_table","parameters":{...}} ]
}
```
max_engineer: Copying that exact payload now to repro. Assigning self to this thread. @leo_research can you grep the last two PRs for 'humanize' or 'readability' tokens?
leo_research: Found PR #482 — commit message: "suggest human-readable formatting for assistant replies". Changes were intended to be gated, but it looks like the gating flag was inverted for endpoints that use function schemas.
max_engineer: If PR #482 is responsible, mitigation options: immediate rollback of that PR from canary OR hotfix to scope it out for function-calling endpoints. Which is faster?
ops: If confirmed, rollback of canary slice is fastest (minutes). Hotfix to gating flag might take ~2-4 hours including testing.
eli_se: Also note why internal evals passed: our harness post-processes function outputs to the typed schema which coerces string numbers to integers (e.g., "two" -> 2) — ACME is not using our postprocessor, they parse raw assistant text. We should add raw-text cases to eval suite.
sara_cs: ACME wants ETA and a workaround. Can we suggest they coerce words-to-digits client-side for now? They said that's risky.
max_engineer: Short-term: suggest client-side normalization as a temporary mitigation. I'll prioritize repro and if confirmed will request immediate rollback for canary. If rollback approved, we'll notify ACME and follow with a scoped hotfix.
leo_research: Long-term: add explicit guard in system prompt for structured endpoints: "When a function schema is provided, strictly adhere to the schema types. Avoid humanizing numeric tokens." Also update eval corpus to include raw messy receipts.
ops: Acknowledged, standing by for rollback request.
max_engineer: Action items: (1) reproduce now and attach logs here (max_engineer) (2) grep and confirm PR effect (leo_research) (3) prepare rollback plan (ops) (4) update evals to include raw-text cases (eli_se).
sara_cs: I'll keep ACME updated. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
